To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
“Myelopoiesic dysregulation associated with a stable APRIL production in MM-infiltrate BM”.

myelopoietic dysregulation characterized in MM patients by a higher proportion of precursor cells is associated to an increased APRIL production by precursor cells, and that APRIL is consumed by MM cells.

1) APRIL expression is upregulated in MM-infiltrating bone marrow; 2) this upregulation is due to an increased proportion of APRIL-producing myeloid precursor cell in the bone marrow; 3) the pool of APRIL producing cells changes upon MM development; and 4) the APRIL produced by precursor cells is consumed by tumor cells.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the dysregulation of the myelopoietic process in MM-infiltrate bone marrow, which results in an increased proportion of APRIL-producing myeloid precursor and in the consumption of APRIL by MM cells, both of which are associated with MM progression.

the role of APRIL in MM pathogenesis, with a particular focus on the myelopoiesic changes occurring in MM-infiltrating BM.

myelopoietic dysregulation in MM patients is characterized by a stable APRIL expression in the bone marrow microenvironment, and that APRIL is consumed by MM cells in the infiltrated BM.
myelopoietic dysregulation associated with a sustained APRIL production is a key event in MM pathogenesis.
